# Run Command Requirements Checklist: One Command to Run Devloops

**Purpose**: Review the quality of the 003 requirements (spec.md, with the plan, research,
data-model, and contracts) before task generation. The focus is loop selection, decisions without
a loop name, pre-run checks, renaming, and init/check changes.
**Created**: 2026-10-09
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are the requirements that the decision commands (`approve`, `replan`, `retry`) apply the same loop-selection and pre-run checks as `devloops run` (FR-005, FR-006) stated, or explicitly excluded? [Gap, Spec §FR-009, §FR-006]
- [x] CHK002 Does the spec define what `--json` prints when the pre-run check stops with exit 30 and no run exists: which keys are present, and whether `run`/`loops` appear at all? [Gap, Spec §FR-006; Contracts cli.md]
- [x] CHK003 Are the 001 and 002 requirements that this feature replaces listed by ID in the spec, rather than only "the requirements this feature replaces"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-018]
- [x] CHK004 Is the content of the amended Principle VI specified in the spec, or is the spec intentionally deferring the wording to research R-12? [Completeness, Spec §FR-019]
- [x] CHK005 Are requirements defined for which loops `status` and the dashboards show for a backend-only run, for example whether frontend-dev is listed as "not used" or omitted? [Gap, Spec §FR-007, §FR-012, §FR-016]
- [x] CHK006 Is the lock behavior (exit 40) for a decision or `run` while another command holds the workspace kept from 001 explicitly, with a [K] reference? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK007 Is "the loop already started there" in FR-005 defined: does a workspace include a loop once its target is recorded (today both targets are recorded when the run starts), or only once that loop's own run starts? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-005]
- [x] CHK008 Is the precedence between a recorded workspace target and an explicit `--backend-target`/`--frontend-target` on a later run specified, including whether the flag is ignored, applied, or refused when it differs? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-005; Spec 001 contracts/cli.md]
- [x] CHK009 Is it stated whether `--target-root` replaces a folder named in `devloops.json` or only fills loops whose project value is present (data-model says it replaces)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005; data-model.md]
- [x] CHK010 Are the exact `status_reason.code` values and messages for the two exit-30 stops fixed in the spec, or delegated to the contract on purpose? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006; research R-3]
- [x] CHK011 Is the `none` answer at the init prompt specified precisely: case-sensitivity, surrounding whitespace, and how to name a folder called `none`? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013; research R-7]
- [x] CHK012 Is "not used by the project" in FR-015 defined as a distinct check status with a name, and is its effect on `ready` and the exit code stated in the spec? [Clarity, Spec §FR-015; data-model.md]
- [x] CHK013 Does FR-004 say whether `--max-trials` persists for later commands or applies only to the command that passes it? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-004; research R-6]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK014 Are the out-of-scope line "no migration" (Scope), the edge case "not supported, start a new workspace", and FR-016 "an `orchestrator/` folder is not read" consistent about what `devloops run` does in such a workspace: refuse, or continue from the loops' own states? [Conflict, Spec §Scope, §Edge Cases, §FR-016]
- [x] CHK015 Is FR-008's "usage error that runs nothing" for `run <loop>` consistent with the no-deprecation decision, and is the error text required to name the new usage or left as the generic parser error? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, Clarifications]
- [x] CHK016 Are the rename rules (FR-016) consistent with the `decision: {command, loop}` JSON field and with `status [loop]` (FR-012), which still expose loop names? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012, §FR-016; Contracts cli.md]
- [x] CHK017 Is US1 scenario 3 (retry continues the run) consistent with the 001 rule that `retry` is refused after `planning-trials-exhausted`, and is that refusal carried over for a run without a loop name? [Consistency, Spec §US1, §FR-009]
- [x] CHK018 Do SC-005 ("no removed command mentioned except in notes") and FR-018 ("edited in place with a note pointing to 003") agree on whether historical text in 001/002 (tasks.md, validation-results.md, research.md) must also change? [Consistency, Spec §SC-005, §FR-018]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK019 Can SC-002 ("no setup lets a frontend trial start without them") be verified objectively, given that a hand-written workspace or a deleted handoff file could bypass the check? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]
- [x] CHK020 Is SC-003's "under 1 second" tied to stated conditions (an existing workspace, a cold start) so it can be checked consistently? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]
- [x] CHK021 Does every functional requirement (FR-001 to FR-019) trace to at least one acceptance scenario, edge case, or success criterion? FR-011, FR-012, and FR-016 have no scenario today. [Traceability, Spec §Requirements]

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK022 Are requirements defined for a backend that completed in an earlier run whose handoff is now stale (the backend target was edited after completion) when a frontend is added later? [Coverage, Edge Case, Spec §FR-007, §US2-4]
- [x] CHK023 Is the behavior specified when the project's backend target is set to `null` after backend-dev completed, and a frontend is then added (FR-005 keeps the backend through the workspace, but this is not stated as a scenario)? [Coverage, Spec §FR-005, §FR-006]
- [x] CHK024 Are recovery requirements specified for `stopped-on-input-error` and `stopped-on-service-error` in the new model, that is, which command resumes them now that `retry` only applies to `stopped-on-failure`? [Coverage, Recovery Flow, Spec §FR-009]
- [x] CHK025 Are the init edge cases covered: `--no-prompt` with one `--no-*` flag and the other target defaulted; `--upgrade` on a project whose `devloops.json` still has both targets set? [Coverage, Spec §FR-013, §FR-014]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK026 Is the assumption "at most one loop waits at a time" justified for every status, including a backend `stopped-on-service-error` while the frontend has its own recorded state from an earlier run? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions, §FR-009]
- [x] CHK027 Is the dependency on the follow-up feature that brings back frontend-only runs recorded with an owner or trigger, so the temporary deviation in FR-019 has an exit condition? [Dependency, Spec §FR-019; plan.md Complexity Tracking]

### Assistant analysis (2026-10-09)

The reviewer chose: CHK008 → usage error; CHK014 → continue and ignore `orchestrator/`; apply the
rest. All recommendations below are now in spec.md (Session 2026-10-09: FR-004, FR-005, FR-005a,
FR-006, FR-009, FR-010, FR-013, FR-015, FR-016a, FR-016b, FR-018, FR-019, SC-002, SC-003, SC-005,
US1 scenarios 7 and 8, Edge Cases, Dependencies), and in research, data-model, and contracts/cli.md.
The markers are left for the reviewer.
